d.g: An intense and unremitting stare.
d.x: He wasn't just handsy, according to the stories. He also used his eyes to grope ('I believe it's called an eye-rape,' one older colleague of mine had noted to me, drily) […]

d.g: Something that is extraordinarily painful to the eyes, such as a psychedelic or rapidly flashing image.
To stare intensely and unremittingly at someone.

eyerape.e: From eye + rape. The second noun sense metaphorically refers to an unwanted assault on a person’s eyes.

d.g: A surname from German.
A triangular peninsula in South Australia.

Eyre Peninsula.e: Named after English explorer Edward John Eyre (1815–1901), who explored parts of the peninsula in 1839–41.

d.g: The corner of the eye
d.x: It [a tear] had many bright sisters, who now are no more, so that it is left solitary in its eyecorner

d.g: A hook with an eye or ring attached.
The hook that goes into the eye of a hook and eye closure.
A village in Raeren municipality, Liège province, Belgium; part of the German-speaking Community of Belgium

Eynatten.e: Borrowed from Dutch Eynatten, possibly from Middle Dutch *enet (“lonely place”).

d.g: To stick googly eyes on (inanimate objects) in public places.
d.x: Ever wondered what Downton’s Lord Grantham would look like with googly eyes? Well even if you didn't he has already been 'eyebombed' by the latest blog to jump on the trend.

d.g: A window.
d.x: A kidcote is a special name for a prison. Some kidcotes don’t even have an eyethurl. What is an eyethurl? An eyethurl is a window such as the one through which the lovely Rapunzel let down her crinets. […] Note: For dretching the curly crineted child with a fearbabe, the killbuck was sent to a kidcote without an eyethurl. […] The hardhewer graffed for stone for a knosp / For the door to his cosh, upsy-English with burl; / He theeked it with thatch and stood back to aimcry, / Then shrieked, “Juvament! Hadivist! No eyethurl!”

eyethurl.e: From eye + thurl (“hole”), a modern calque of Old English ēagþyrel. Popularized by Susan Kelz Sperling’s 1977 book Poplollies and Bellibones: A Celebration of Lost Words (see quotation).

d.g: In an eyeing manner.
d.x: It would seem that the devil employs all his energies in Rome at misrepresentation and falsehood, and eyeingly awaits a papal word as would a dog a bone from the table of his master.

d.g: Individual lashes that are applied to the natural lash using a semipermanent glue.
d.x: She’s wearing false eyelashes, or perhaps she gets eyelash extensions. Where her cheeks were once angular, they are now a bit sunken.

d.g: A gay man who derives sexual pleasure from observing other people, especially when they are engaging in a sexual activity.

eyeball queen.e: From eyeball + queen (“an effeminate or homosexual man”).

d.g: To stand by idly without helping or contributing.
The practice of standing by idly without helping or contributing.
The practice of lowering one's eyes before gazing left or right, to avoid a shifty expression on camera.
d.x: Media coaches recommend that speakers on TV programs use eye bounce, in which the eyes do not move horizontally. Instead, the speaker first looks down […]

d.g: A plastic surgical procedure to alter the appearance of the eyelid(s), especially for cosmetic reasons.
d.x:
“You don’t look too bad, you know. If you got an eye job you could pass for thirty. Easy.”
At least she didn’t have bags under her eyes the way he did. And no one had ever told her before that she needed an eye job. The nerve of the man!

eye job.e: From eye + job, after nose job.

d.g: A device consisting of a sink with two upward-facing faucets, used for eyewashing.
d.x: Eye washers should be of the dish washing sprayer type, although other types are available. Eye washer requirements in areas other than laboratories may be satisfied with the use of standard eye washer units.

d.g: The wasp nest beetle, Metoecus paradoxus.

eyelash bug.e: From this insect's antennae which look like human eyelashes, coined in 2020 when American rapper Megan Thee Stallion created an Instagram post featuring a video in which Megan's friend asks what a bug on the wall is and Megan responds with, "bitch, an eyelash bug [sic]," and the two laugh. Later on, people in the comments identified the insect as M. paradoxus However, the bug in the video appears to be a male Pterotus obscuripennis instead.

d.g: Variant of eyepatch.
Variant of eyeshadow.
